helpIntro.message: SideBrowser · A browser in your sidebar.

helpLanguage.message: The interface language follows Chrome automatically.

helpStartNavigation.message: Click the SideBrowser extension icon to open the sidebar. Enter an address or Google search term and press Enter. Use “Open current page” to open the active tab’s address in the sidebar.

helpStartShortcut.message: Right-click a page or link and choose “Open in SideBrowser” for quick access. View or change your keyboard shortcut in Settings. Drag the sidebar edge to adjust its width.

helpStatePersistence.message: Your sidebar page stays open when you switch tabs or close the source tab. Each browser window can have its own sidebar page.

helpStateRestore.message: After closing the sidebar or browser, reopening restores the saved address. Unsaved form input, playback progress, and other live page state may be lost.

helpMobileViewport.message: Switch between mobile and desktop modes in Settings or the sidebar’s “⋯” menu. Mobile mode suits a narrow sidebar and still supports your mouse and scroll wheel. The layout depends on the website.

helpEmbeddingLimits.message: If a page loads slowly, try reloading it. Some websites, sign-in flows, or videos may not work in the sidebar. Use “⋯” to open the current page in a new tab.

helpPrivacy.message: Preferences, recently opened addresses and titles, and addresses and navigation history used to restore pages are stored on your device and are not uploaded to the developer. Clearing recently opened entries only removes that list; it does not delete saved page addresses, navigation history, or website data. Websites and search providers have their own privacy policies.

settingsIntro.message: Manage your browsing preferences. Changes are saved automatically.

settingsModeDescription.message: Shared across all windows. Switching modes reloads the page in every open sidebar.

settingsShortcutDescription.message: Open the active tab in the sidebar. You can change this shortcut in Chrome.

settingsRecentDescription.message: Keep your last 10 explicitly opened addresses for easy access. Clearing the list does not close your page or sign you out of websites.

settingsClearConfirmation.message: Clear all recently opened entries? This cannot be undone.

errorSettingsOnly.message: Open SideBrowser settings to perform this action.

helpRecent.message: Click the clock in the address bar to see recently opened pages. Select an entry to reopen it, remove individual entries, or clear the list. The list is shared across windows and stays available after restarting your browser.

helpFeedbackDescription.message: Found a problem or have an idea? Let us know on GitHub.
